question: What will Amazon report as its Q3 2026 net sales?

calls.reasoning: Guidance $197-202B (assumes -80bps FX; Prime Day shifted out of Q3, ~400bps drag). Amazon historically reports at or slightly above the top of guidance (median ~+0.5B over top; range ~-0.7 to +3.7B). Consensus ~202-204.6B; HSBC 203.3B on AWS ~37% growth. Median 203.2B. Downside: stronger dollar or retail softness; upside: AWS acceleration. No human market on revenue found; Polymarket has an EPS-beat market (reported 62%) only — not a match. Capex markets irrelevant.
calls.dossier:
- Amazon Q2 2026 8-K (Jul 30 2026): Q3 2026 net sales guided $197.0-202.0B (9-12% YoY vs Q3'25 $180.17B); 'Excluding the impact of Prime Day in both 2025 and 2026, Q3 YoY growth would be nearly 400bps higher'; guidance assumes ~80bps unfavorable FX. Op income guide $22.5-26.5B.
- Q2 2026 net sales $200.6B (+20% YoY ex-FX; FX +$0.1B); AWS +37% (~$42.2B) (8-K, Jul 2026).
- Consensus estimates vary: ~$202.1-202.2B (MarketBeat/others), ~$204.1B (Bitget citing market estimate, Jul 2026), ~$204.6B (some aggregators, Oct 2026).
- HSBC (techflowpost, 2026): Q3 revenue forecast $203.3B, AWS $45.1B (+36.8%); expects above top of guidance.
- Analysts broadly expect AWS +30-35% YoY in Q3 (fool.com Oct 16 2026).
- History (from memory of releases): actual vs guidance top — Q3'24 158.9 vs 158.5; Q4'24 187.8 vs 188.5; Q1'25 155.7 vs 155.5; Q2'25 167.7 vs 164.0; Q3'25 180.2 vs 179.5; Q4'25 213.4 vs 213.0; Q2'26 200.6 vs 199.0. Revenue surprise vs consensus +1% to +2.4% over last 4 quarters (question background).
- Risks both ways: USD moves during Jul-Sep 2026 vs guidance FX assumption (not found); retail demand; AWS capacity additions.
- Status quo: report at/near top of guidance range.
- Resolves off headline consolidated 'Net sales' in Q3 2026 earnings release (Oct 29 2026), not ex-FX or segments.
- Event window: quarter Jul 1 -> Sep 30 2026 (100% elapsed); release Oct 29 2026.
- Searched, absent: Q3 2026 USD index change vs guidance assumption; human prediction market on Q3 revenue (only EPS-beat market on Polymarket).

The Prime Day shift (Q3 2025 to Q2 2026) cuts reported Q3 growth by about 4 points, but underlying growth (~16%) and AWS at 37% support a beat over the guide top. The dollar strengthened in September, so FX may hurt slightly more than the -80bp built into guidance; the large past beats came in quarters with a weakening dollar. calls.reference_class: Amazon quarterly net sales actual minus top of guidance, Q1 2025-Q2 2026

calls.reasoning: Reference class: Amazon's reported net sales compared with the top of its own guidance. Over the last 8 quarters it came in above the top 7 times, by -0.7 to +3.7B (median about +0.5B, mean about +1.2B). The Q3 2026 guidance is $197-202B. It already accounts for the Prime Day shift into Q2 (about 400bp drag) and about 80bp of FX headwind. The dollar was roughly flat over the quarter and firmer in September, so there is no big FX tailwind like the ones behind the large beats in Q2'25 and Q1'26. AWS growing around 37% supports a beat of about +1B over the guide top. Consensus is about $202-204.6B. Median is 203.3. No human market prices Q3 revenue. The Polymarket capex and EPS-beat contracts do not match this question, and nothing plausible would push the figure outside 194-212.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the guidance ($197-202B), the Prime Day shift, the ~80bp FX assumption, and that Amazon usually lands above the guide top. Disputes: (1) Q1'26 beat size. Run 3 and Run 2 put it at about +3B; Run 1 left that quarter out. I accept about +3B, which raises the mean beat but not the median. (2) FX. Run 2 says the dollar strengthened in September; Run 3 says DXY was +0.35% over the quarter with EUR flat. These are compatible: the late-quarter strengthening was small and partly offset earlier in the quarter. Net FX is about in line with guidance, so there is no tailwind and at most a slight headwind. That argues against assuming another +3B beat. (3) The consensus figures differ ($202.1B vs $204.6B) across aggregators and dates. I could not settle this without web access, so I treat consensus as a band. Judgment: I take a guide top +1.3B median, which sits between Run 2's and Run 3's readings, because the beat history with no FX tailwind points there, not because I averaged them. I widened the tails a little for retail and FX risk. I retrieved nothing myself.
